newsitem.title: TURKEY: Trade body to halt Mersin exports unless fees cut.
newsitem.headline: Trade body to halt Mersin exports unless fees cut.

text.p: Turkey's southern exporters union said on Wednesday they were planning to halt exports from Mersin port, Turkey's largest trade port, unless the government reduced port service prices, recently raised by up to 170 percent.

"We are going to stop all export from Mersin port if the government does not reduce port service prices," said Mahmut Arslan, head of the Mediterranean Grain and Pulses Exporters Union, based in Mersin.
The stoppage would take effect from May 6, he told Reuters.
"The TCDD (Turkish Railways Authority) has raised prices of port services to $8.3 per tonne from $5 and empty container services to $35 per tonne from $13," he said.
Mersin port, one of the seven ports operated by the TCDD, handles about 11 million tonnes of incoming and outgoing cargo every year, one million tonnes of that being pulses.

Arslan said the union, which comprises exporters from Adana, Mersin, Hatay and Gaziantep provinces, had appealed to the transport ministry but had not received any reply to their demand that the fees be lowered to their original levels to compete with other ports in the nearby countries.
"If we lose the competitive edge, Turkey's income from the Mersin port will be diverted to Latakia of Syria or Dumyat in Egypt, which both offer cheaper services," he said.
He said about $9 billion, or one-sixth, of Turkey's entire annual trade was carried through Mersin port last year.

"Turkey will lose on its revenues. Its export have already been floundering. The government will lose income from Mersin port on exports of $2 billion and imports of up to $7 billion a year," he said.
He said the fees, raised in February, would undermine plans to boost Turkey's entire exports to $28 billion in 1997 from an estimated $20 billion in 1996.
"The rise in prices have equalised cost of port services for export and imports whereas traditionally exports should be cheaper as part of government incentives," he said.
He said exporters unions in other areas like Izmir and Istanbul might plan similar actions to draw the government's attention to the issue.
